newsitem.title: PERU: Peru passes amnesty law for jailed general.
newsitem.headline: Peru passes amnesty law for jailed general.

text.p: The Peruvian Congress unanimously approved on Thursday President Alberto Fujimori's amnesty bill obliging the military to release retired general Rodolfo Robles, jailed last week for insubordination.
"The passage of the bill means that the military cannot do what they want," opposition legislator Rafael Rey said during a four-hour debate.
Robles' detention nine days ago brought a tide of public protest that obliged Fujimori to confront the military with a hastily-proposed bill overruling the arrest.
Defence Minister Tomas Castillo Meza has said the military will accept Congress' decision, and Robles is now scheduled to be released on Saturday once the law comes into effect.
"The freedom of the general is an answer to the legitimate demands of the people," said opposition legislator Javier Alva Orlandini.
"General Robles is defending the noble ideals of Peruvian democracy and human rights."

In what witnesses described as more like a kidnapping, the military arrested Robles in a Lima street last week in response to his claims that an army "death-squad" took part in the recent bombing of a local television station.
Robles has frequently spoken out against Peru's military, which has maintained a delicate balance of power with Fujimori since his 1990 election.

After claiming an army "death squad" killed 10 students and a university teacher in 1992, he went into exile in Argentina to avoid trial but later returned to Peru when the government granted him an amnesty.

Fujimori's amnesty for Robles was widely applauded within Peru and is expected to help him in the polls, where his traditionally high approval rating has slipped to around 50 percent in recent months.
"There is a courage in Fujimori's attitude that should be recognised by his adversaries," wrote Manuel D'Ornellas in an editorial for the daily Expreso.
"Here, what was at stake was up to what point the executive was prepared to pander the whims of a spoiled military."
